title: SmoothShip: automated upgrade scheduler and rollout circuit-breakers for Private deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an automated, policy-driven upgrade scheduler for Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) that orchestrates phased migrations with built-in circuit-breakers and observability. The system (SmoothShip) schedules cohorts, verifies compatibility preflight, runs transactional data migration hooks where required, and enforces automatic rollback on safety violations. This ticket covers design, implementation of the scheduler, rollout gate primitives, and integration with existing upgrade agent and telemetry pipelines.
background: Customers running Private installations require predictable upgrade windows and minimal disruption. Current private upgrade flows are manual or semi-automated and require operator intervention for cohort selection, preflight checks, and rollback decisions. As we expand LTS channel support and stricter compliance SLAs, we need a deterministic orchestration layer that encodes safety gates and version compatibility policies and can operate across air-gapped and VPC environments.
goals: Provide a scheduler that can plan staggered cohort upgrades across an account fleet based on policy (region, size, LTS channel)
Enforce rollout gates: preflight, canary probe, steady-state evaluation, and automated circuit-breaker rollback
Support transactional migration hooks and idempotent resume/rollback semantics for on-prem stateful components
Integrate audit logs and operator override controls for enterprise compliance
Expose upgrade plan and telemetry to Console and to the existing upgrade agent for execution
non_goals: Replace the runtime orchestration engine — this ticket will integrate with the current agent and conductor
Implement new kernel-level migration tooling — that belongs to runtime/inference teams
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can create a cohort plan for >1000 hosts with configurable concurrency and cooling windows
Preflight compatibility checks (schema, binary compatibility, config validation) run and block plan if failing
Automated circuit-breaker triggers rollback when service error rate increases >3x baseline or latency P99 doubles for >5 minutes
Stateful migration hooks support transactional resume with at-most-once semantics in simulated network partitions
All actions are logged to audit trail with immutable identifiers and retained per project retention policy
Console shows per-cohort status and timeline; operators can pause/resume and opt-into manual approval gates
design_notes: Scheduler core: deterministic job planner that uses account policies + signal-driven scaling to compute cohort buckets
Cohort selection: tags (region, LTS-channel, criticality), weight-based sampling for canaries, and customer opt-out lists
Rollout gates: archetype = [preflight, canary-run, hold-window, ramp, finalization]; each gate has success criteria and timeout
Circuit-breaker: pluggable evaluation functions (error rate, latency, dependent service health). Default thresholds provided, customizable per-customer
Migration hooks: small DSL for declaring pre/post migration steps (db-migrate, kv-snapshot, leader-evacuation) with retry policies and idempotency tokens
Backoff and pause semantics: exponential backoff with cohort-level pause and global abort if >N cohorts fail concurrently
On-prem constraints: scheduler communicates plans to customer-controlled agent over outbound-only channel; it must support air-gapped by delivering bundle + signed plan via S3/drive import
implementation_plan: Phase 1: API and scheduler prototype (manager that computes cohorts and persists plans to upgraded-plans store)
Phase 2: Implement gate primitives and circuit-breaker evaluator; integrate with telemetry pipeline for real-time signals
Phase 3: Build migration hook DSL and extend agent to understand plan execution and idempotent resume
Phase 4: Console integration (plan visualizer, manual overrides, per-cohort logs), and RBAC controls
Phase 5: Canary with internal customers -> staged customer rollouts -> GA
rollout_plan: Internal canary: pick 3 non-critical private clusters and run full upgrade using SmoothShip with manual oversight
Beta customers: opt-in cohort for customers on non-LTS early channels, run limited concurrency
GA: enable by default for Private accounts with override and opt-out lists
Support: ship runbook and on-call escalation path; provide per-customer dry-run reports
testing_plan: Unit tests for scheduler heuristics and gate evaluation functions
Integration tests simulating network partitions, agent disconnects, and mid-migration failures
Chaos test: intentionally fail dependent services and verify circuit-breaker behavior
Large-scale simulation: synthetic fleet of 10k nodes to validate planning performance and concurrency limits
Security review and static analysis on plan signing and bundle delivery paths
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: per-plan throughput, cohorts completed, average time per gate, rollback counts
Alerts: Plan-level critical alert when circuit-breaker triggers or >3 cohorts abort in 24h
SLOs: median upgrade time per node, successful upgrade rate target >= 99% within 48h window
Audit stream: forward plan and step events to retention bucket and to customer-specified SIEM when configured
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental mass rollout due to bad cohort selector. Mitigation: dry-run mode, mandatory canary and operator approval for >100 nodes
Risk: incompatibility with custom on-prem configs. Mitigation: enhanced preflight validators and customer-provided config test harness
Risk: audit/forensics gaps. Mitigation: immutable event log with HMAC-signed entries; integrate with KMS
Risk: air-gapped delivery complexity. Mitigation: signed plan bundles and verification tool built into agent; docs and automation for offline import
notes_and_decisions: Decision: use existing upgrade-agent protocol for execution and extend it with plan-token handshake instead of building a new transport
Decision: default circuit-breaker thresholds will be conservative; customers may supply overrides in their policy manifest
Open: finalize DSL syntax for migration hooks (proposal under /confluence/PrivateUpgrade/migration-dsl)
customer_notes: Customers will be able to preview full upgrade plan in Console before initiating; dry-run artifacts include preflight report and risk score
For regulated customers we will enable mandatory manual approval gates and extended audit retention
next_steps: Finalize migration hook DSL and document examples (db snapshot, leader eviction, config migration)
Ship scheduler prototype and start internal canary (owner: Ethan Kim)
Schedule security review with Lina Gomez and complete design sign-off
